temptingClaims: Length contraction is what a camera would see.
whyTempting: § 4 says the moving body's length along the motion appears shortened, and a photograph is the everyday meaning of how something appears.
whereItIsTrue: In the paper's own sense: the positions of the body's points, taken at one time of the resting system K, lie on an ellipsoid shortened along the motion in the ratio \(1 : \sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}\) (p. 903).

whatIsTrue.r0: § 4 finds the shape of a moving body from where its points are at one instant of the resting system's time. A camera records light that arrives together, which left different parts of the body at different times. That is a different question, and the paper does not treat it.
whatIsTrue.r1: The paper takes a rigid sphere of radius \(R\) at rest in the moving system k and writes its surface in the coordinates of K at the time \(t=0\): \(\frac{x^2}{\left(\sqrt{1-\left(\frac{v}{V}\right)^2}\right)^2}+y^2+z^2=R^2\), an ellipsoid of revolution with the axes \(R\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}\), \(R\), \(R\) (p. 903). Every point is taken at the same time of K, read from K's clocks synchronized as § 1 prescribes, so the shortening is a statement about simultaneous positions. A photograph gathers the light that reaches the lens at one moment; light from the far side of a moving body left it earlier than light from the near side, so a picture combines positions from different times, and what it shows needs its own calculation. SR-03's moving-sphere preset gives the paper's ellipsoid, axes 0.8, 1 and 1 for \(R=1\) at \(v=0.6\,V\), and its manifest lists optical camera appearance among what it does not model.
whatIsTrue.r2: (1) In k, where the sphere rests, its surface is a sphere of radius \(R\). (2) The equations of § 3 carry k's coordinates into K's; fix one time of K, \(t=0\), and the surface becomes \(\frac{x^2}{1-(v/V)^2}+y^2+z^2=R^2\). (3) Its axes are \(R\sqrt{1-(v/V)^2}\) along the motion and \(R\) across it. (4) At \(v=0.6\,V\): \(\sqrt{1-0.36}=0.8\), so the axes are \(0.8\,R\), \(R\), \(R\). (5) These are positions taken at one time of K. Light reaching an eye or a lens together left the body at different times, so a picture is a different object, which the paper does not compute.
whatIsTrue.r3: What a camera or an eye would record of a fast-moving body was taken up in 1959 in J. Terrell's 'Invisibility of the Lorentz Contraction' and R. Penrose's 'The apparent shape of a relativistically moving sphere', whose titles state their subject. This record has not read them and gives no account of their results.

sources: A. Einstein, Ann. Phys. (4) 17, 891–921 (1905), plate p. 903
